title: Checks to see if all common metadata is defined in Cargo.toml.
summary: See: https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/documentation.html#cargotoml-includes-all-common-metadata-c-metadata It will be more difficult for users to discover the purpose of the crate, and key information related to it. Clippy puts this lint in the cargo group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for calls to ends_with with possible file extensions and suggests to use a case-insensitive approach instead.
summary: ends_with is case-sensitive and may not detect files with a valid extension. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of the abs() method that cast the result to unsigned.
summary: The unsigned_abs() method avoids panic when called on the MIN value. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for casts from an enum tuple constructor to an integer.
summary: The cast is easily confused with casting a c-like enum value to an integer. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for casts from an enum type to an integral type that will definitely truncate the value.
summary: The resulting integral value will not match the value of the variant it came from. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for casts between numeric types that can be replaced by safe conversion functions.
summary: Rust’s as keyword will perform many kinds of conversions, including silently lossy conversions. Conversion functions such as i32::from will only perform lossless conversions. Using the conversion functions prevents conversions from becoming silently lossy if the input types ever change, and makes it clear for people reading the code that the conversion is lossless. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for a known NaN float being cast to an integer
summary: NaNs are cast into zero, so one could simply use this and make the code more readable. The lint could also hint at a programmer error. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for casts between numeric types that may truncate large values.
summary: This is expected behavior, so the cast is Allow by default. It suggests user either explicitly ignore the lint, or use try_from() and handle the truncation, default, or panic explicitly. In some problem domains, it is good practice to avoid truncation. This lint can be activated to help assess where additional checks could be beneficial. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for casts from an unsigned type to a signed type of the same size, or possibly smaller due to target-dependent integers.
summary: Performing such a cast is a no-op for the compiler (that is, nothing is changed at the bit level), and the binary representation of the value is reinterpreted. This can cause wrapping if the value is too big for the target signed type. However, the cast works as defined, so this lint is Allow by default. While such a cast is not bad in itself, the results can be surprising when this is not the intended behavior: Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for casts from any numeric type to a float type where the receiving type cannot store all values from the original type without rounding errors.
summary: This possible rounding is to be expected, so this lint is Allow by default. It’s not bad at all. But in some applications it can be helpful to know where precision loss can take place. This lint can help find those places in the code. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for casts, using as or pointer::cast, from a less strictly aligned pointer to a more strictly aligned pointer.
summary: Dereferencing the resulting pointer may be undefined behavior. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for casts from a signed to an unsigned numeric type.
summary: In this case, negative values wrap around to large positive values, which can be quite surprising in practice. However, since the cast works as defined, this lint is Allow by default. Possibly surprising results. You can activate this lint as a one-time check to see where numeric wrapping can arise. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for as casts between raw pointers to slices with differently sized elements.
summary: The produced raw pointer to a slice does not update its length metadata. The produced pointer will point to a different number of bytes than the original pointer because the length metadata of a raw slice pointer is in elements rather than bytes. Producing a slice reference from the raw pointer will either create a slice with less data (which can be surprising) or create a slice with more data and cause Undefined Behavior. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for a raw slice being cast to a slice pointer
summary: This can result in multiple &mut references to the same location when only a pointer is required. ptr::slice_from_raw_parts is a safe alternative that doesn’t require the same safety requirements to be upheld. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.
